blocks: ## Choose your route and revision goal

This page is a rich revision chapter rather than a one-period script. Use the Core route to secure the clock system, then move into Develop and Stretch for minutes, schedules, daily routines and more precise expressions.
### Core
- Ask and answer كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ .
- Tell all twelve o’clock times.
- Use quarter, half and twenty past.
### Develop
- Use إِلَّا for times to the hour.
- Say exact minutes.
- Add morning, afternoon and evening.
### Stretch
- Compare analogue, digital and 24-hour time.
- Describe a full timetable.
- Explain common listening traps.
[callout] How to use this chapter Revise one teaching cycle, complete one skills task, then play at least one Explorer or Builder game. Return later for Scholar and Mastery challenges.
### Objectives
- Ask and answer كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ for all twelve hours Speaking
- Tell times past the hour with وَالنِّصْفُ، وَالرُّبُعُ، وَالثُّلُثُ and minutes Listening
- Tell times to the hour using إِلَّا Reading
- Add صَبَاحًا / مَسَاءً and write times in full sentences about your day Writing
### Success Criteria
- 🟢 I can say every o’clock time from 1:00 to 12:00 with the correct feminine ordinal.
- 🟠 I can build times like 4:30, 9:15 and 6:20 using the وَ + fraction formula.
- 🟧 I can decode الخَامِسَةُ إِلَّا رُبُعًا as 4:45 — naming the coming hour, not the one just passed.

[callout] Why this matters in the exam Times are a common detail in listening tasks: train departures, TV programmes, opening hours and appointments. A frequent listening trap is إِلَّا — students hear الخَامِسَةُ and write 5:45 when the answer is 4:45 . By the end of today, that trap won’t work on you.
## The twelve hours — كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟

To ask the time, say كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ (“How much is the hour?”). To answer, Arabic says “the hour the third” for 3 o’clock — the noun السَّاعَةُ followed by an ordinal from Lesson 1. And because سَاعَةٌ is feminine , every single clock ordinal is feminine. One rule, twelve hours, zero exceptions.
### Vocabulary O’clock, one to twelve

TABLE: Time | بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ | Literally // 1:00 | السَّاعَةُ الوَاحِدَةُ | “the hour the one” — ⚠️ NOT الأُولَى ! // 2:00 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ | the second hour // 3:00 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ | the third hour // 4:00 | السَّاعَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ | the fourth hour // 5:00 | السَّاعَةُ الخَامِسَةُ | the fifth hour // 6:00 | السَّاعَةُ السَّادِسَةُ | the sixth hour // 7:00 | السَّاعَةُ السَّابِعَةُ | the seventh hour // 8:00 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ | the eighth hour // 9:00 | السَّاعَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ | the ninth hour // 10:00 | السَّاعَةُ العَاشِرَةُ | the tenth hour // 11:00 | السَّاعَةُ الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ | the eleventh hour // 12:00 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ | the twelfth hour
[callout] Asking the time — three ways كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ What time is it? فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ؟ At what time…? مَتَى؟ When?
[callout] The 1 o’clock trap One o’clock is السَّاعَةُ الوَاحِدَةُ , using the counting word — never الأُولَى (“the first”). Think of it as “hour number one”, not “the first hour”.

## Past the hour — وَالنِّصْفُ وَالرُّبُعُ وَالثُّلُثُ

To add minutes past the hour, Arabic simply says وَ (“and”) plus a fraction. And here Arabic has a weapon English lacks: الثُّلُثُ — “the third of an hour” — a single elegant word for twenty minutes .
### Vocabulary Fractions of the hour

TABLE: الكَلِمَةُ | Meaning | Minutes // النِّصْفُ | the half | 30 // الرُّبُعُ | the quarter (¼) | 15 // الثُّلُثُ | the third (⅓) — Arabic’s secret weapon! | 20 // دَقِيقَةٌ / دَقَائِقُ | minute / minutes | 1+ // ثَانِيَةٌ / ثَوَانٍ | second / seconds | —
[callout] The formula السَّاعَةُ + hour + وَ + fraction/minutes 4:30 = السَّاعَةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالنِّصْفُ · 9:15 = السَّاعَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَالرُّبُعُ · 6:20 = السَّاعَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالثُّلُثُ

[callout] Exact minutes — Lesson 1 returns! 3:05 = السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَخَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ · 8:10 = السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَعَشْرُ دَقَائِقَ Spot the golden rule at work: دَقِيقَةٌ is feminine, so 5 and 10 drop the ة — خَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ، عَشْرُ دَقَائِقَ . Your Lesson 1 grammar just earned you Listening marks.
Related game practice
### Game 3 — Past or To?
## The إِلَّا trick — minutes TO the hour

Here is the most elegant idea in the whole lesson. For “quarter to five”, Arabic looks forward to the coming hour and subtracts: “the hour five, except a quarter” . The word إِلَّا means “except” — the same word you may know from لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللهُ (“there is no god except Allah”). One small word, doing beautiful mathematical work.
### The formula Name the NEXT hour, then subtract

TABLE: Time | بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ | Think: literally… // 4:45 | السَّاعَةُ الخَامِسَةُ إِلَّا رُبُعًا | “hour five, except a quarter” // 7:40 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ إِلَّا ثُلُثًا | “hour eight, except a third (20 min)” // 9:50 | السَّاعَةُ العَاشِرَةُ إِلَّا عَشْرَ دَقَائِقَ | “hour ten, except ten minutes” // 2:55 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَ دَقَائِقَ | “hour three, except five minutes” // 12:45 | السَّاعَةُ الوَاحِدَةُ إِلَّا رُبُعًا | “hour one, except a quarter” — it wraps around!

[callout] The examiner’s favourite trap 🪤 You hear الخَامِسَةُ إِلَّا رُبُعًا and your pen wants to write 5:45. Stop. إِلَّا means minutes are subtracted : hour five MINUS a quarter = 4:45 . Train the reflex: hear إِلَّا → the real time is before the hour you heard.

[callout] Grammar whisper 🤫 After إِلَّا the fraction changes its ending: الرُّبُعُ → إِلَّا رُبُعًا ، الثُّلُثُ → إِلَّا ثُلُثًا . You don’t need to know why yet (it’s the accusative case — a later grammar topic). Just copy the pattern faithfully: illā rubʿan, illā thuluthan .
## Morning, evening & full sentences — صَبَاحًا وَمَسَاءً
Arabic uses a 12-hour clock in speech, so you need the little words that replace a.m. and p.m. — then you can drop your times into real sentences about your day.
### Vocabulary Parts of the day & precision words

TABLE: الكَلِمَةُ | Meaning | Example // صَبَاحًا | in the morning (a.m.) | السَّابِعَةُ صَبَاحًا = 7 a.m. // ظُهْرًا | at noon | الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ ظُهْرًا = 12 noon // بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ | in the afternoon | الرَّابِعَةُ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ = 4 p.m. // مَسَاءً | in the evening (p.m.) | الثَّامِنَةُ مَسَاءً = 8 p.m. // لَيْلًا | at night | الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ لَيْلًا = 11 at night // تَمَامًا | exactly / on the dot | الخَامِسَةُ تَمَامًا = 5:00 sharp // تَقْرِيبًا | approximately | السَّادِسَةُ تَقْرِيبًا = about 6

[callout] Building sentences — the “at” pattern To say something happens at a time, use فِي السَّاعَةِ… أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ صَبَاحًا. — I wake up at 7 a.m. تَبْدَأُ المَدْرَسَةُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ إِلَّا رُبُعًا. — School starts at 8:45. أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ العَاشِرَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ لَيْلًا. — I sleep at 10:30 at night. 🔍 Sharp eyes will spot the ordinal’s last vowel change after فِي ( السَّابِعَةِ not السَّابِعَةُ ) — that’s the genitive case saying hello. Copy the pattern; mastery comes later.

[callout] Heritage link 🕌 — the original timetable A prayer timetable is authentic Arabic reading material you use every week! Sample London times: الفَجْرُ: ٤:٤٥ صَبَاحًا · الظُّهْرُ: ١:١٥ · العَصْرُ: ٥:٣٠ · المَغْرِبُ: ٩:٢٠ مَسَاءً · العِشَاءُ: ١٠:٤٥ . Challenge: say each one aloud in full words — المَغْرِبُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ وَالثُّلُثِ مَسَاءً . 🎙️

## How time connects with the Numbers strand
### Lesson 1 · Numbers
[ar] السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ
Clock hours depend on feminine ordinal forms.
### Lesson 3 · Age
[ar] عُمْرِي خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
The same number forms appear in personal information.
### Lesson 4 · Money
[ar] المَوْعِدُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ
Appointments and shopping times combine numbers with real-life tasks.
### Lesson 6 · Date
[ar] يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ
Dates and times combine to form schedules and notices.
## Read, listen, speak and write with time
### Reading Daily timetable

[ar] أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ صَبَاحًا. يَبْدَأُ الدَّرْسُ الأَوَّلُ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ إِلَّا رُبُعًا. أَتَنَاوَلُ الغَدَاءَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الوَاحِدَةِ وَخَمْسِ دَقَائِقَ، وَأَعُودُ إِلَى البَيْتِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ وَعَشْرِ دَقَائِقَ.
- What time does the speaker wake up?
- When does the first lesson begin?
- What time is lunch?
- When does the speaker return home?
### Listening Schedule announcements
Listen without looking first. Write the three times you hear.

[ar] ١. يُغَادِرُ القِطَارُ إِلَى لَنْدَنَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ مَسَاءً. ٢. يَبْدَأُ الفِيلْمُ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ إِلَّا رُبُعًا. ٣. يَفْتَحُ المَتْحَفُ أَبْوَابَهُ فِي السَّاعَةِ العَاشِرَةِ إِلَّا عَشْرَ دَقَائِقَ صَبَاحًا.
### Speaking My daily rhythm
Give a short spoken description containing at least six times:
- waking up;
- starting school or work;
- a break or meal;
- finishing;
- an evening activity;
- bedtime.
[callout] Challenge Include one “past”, one “to”, one exact-minute expression and one time with صَبَاحًا or مَسَاءً .
### Writing My timetable
Write 7–9 Arabic sentences describing a school day or weekend schedule.
Word count: 0
### Stretch Digital and 24-hour time

TABLE: Digital | Natural Arabic | 24-hour context // 07:45 | السَّاعَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ إِلَّا رُبُعًا صَبَاحًا | often written ٠٧:٤٥ // 13:20 | السَّاعَةُ الوَاحِدَةُ وَالثُّلُثُ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ | often written ١٣:٢٠ // 18:30 | السَّاعَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالنِّصْفُ مَسَاءً | often written ١٨:٣٠ // 21:05 | السَّاعَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ وَخَمْسُ دَقَائِقَ لَيْلًا | often written ٢١:٠٥
Related game practice
### Game 7 — Timetable Information Hunt
## Times in the real exam — الوَقْتُ فِي الاِمْتِحَانِ
Three disguises again: timetables in Reading, announcements in Listening, and your daily routine in Speaking and Writing.
### Task A · Reading 📖 The school timetable — جَدْوَلُ الحِصَصِ

TABLE: الحِصَّةُ (lesson) | الوَقْتُ // اللُّغَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ | ٩:٠٠ – ١٠:٠٠ // الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ (Maths) | ١٠:١٥ – ١١:١٥ // التَّرْبِيَةُ الإِسْلَامِيَّةُ | ١١:٣٠ – ١٢:٣٠ // الاِسْتِرَاحَةُ (break) | ١٢:٣٠ – ١:١٥ // العُلُومُ (Science) | ١:١٥ – ٢:١٥
- What time does Arabic start? Answer in Arabic words.
- Which lesson begins at الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ ?
- How long is the break — in Arabic, using a fraction word?
- Science ends at 2:15. Say it in Arabic words.
- فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ تَمَامًا — at nine o’clock exactly.
- التَّرْبِيَةُ الإِسْلَامِيَّةُ — Islamic Studies (11:30).
- 45 minutes = ثَلَاثَةُ أَرْبَاعِ سَاعَةٍ (“three quarters of an hour”) — or simply خَمْسٌ وَأَرْبَعُونَ دَقِيقَةً .
- فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ وَالرُّبُعِ — at quarter past two.
### Task B · Listening 🎧 Station announcements
Listen without looking first. Ask a partner or reader to say each announcement twice , then write the time in digits.
### Task C · Speaking & Writing ✍️ My day in five times — يَوْمِي
Say, then write, five sentences about your day. Each must use a different time pattern: exact hour · وَالنِّصْفُ · وَالرُّبُعُ · إِلَّا · minutes.

[callout] Scaffold أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ ______ . أُصَلِّي الفَجْرَ فِي السَّاعَةِ ______ . تَبْدَأُ المَدْرَسَةُ فِي السَّاعَةِ ______ . أَتَنَاوَلُ العَشَاءَ فِي السَّاعَةِ ______ . أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ ______ . (I wake up at… · I pray Fajr at… · School starts at… · I eat dinner at… · I sleep at…)

## Learn by reading clocks, decoding phrases and repairing errors
Each preserved game now appears beside the language point it practises.
## Choose your challenge
Pick one level. Due next lesson via Teams Assignments. ✍️
### 🟢 Mild
Draw eight clock faces showing: 3:00 · 7:30 · 9:15 · 1:00 · 6:20 · 4:45 · 10:50 · 12:00. Label each in fully vowelled Arabic words (use this lesson’s tables as your word bank).
### 🟠 Spicy
Write six sentences about your real school day. You must use وَالنِّصْفُ , وَالرُّبُعُ , وَالثُّلُثُ and إِلَّا at least once each, plus صَبَاحًا or مَسَاءً twice.
### 🟧 Hot

Find this week’s prayer timetable for your city. Write all five prayer times in full Arabic words with صَبَاحًا / مَسَاءً , then add two comparison sentences (e.g. صَلَاةُ الفَجْرِ قَبْلَ صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ ) — a preview of next lesson’s comparatives!
## 🎮 Beat the Clock — اِقْرَأِ السَّاعَةَ!
The clock sets itself to a random time — your job is to pick the correct Arabic. Eight rounds. 👥 Play as teams in breakout rooms, or 🖥️ whole-class with hands up. Can anyone get 8/8?

Eight questions, everything mixed. 6+ means the success criteria are yours. 💬 Scores in the chat!
